headline: Arsenal survive Leeds scare; Liverpool-City looms at Anfield
paragraphs: Arsenal's best-corroborated story of the day was a routine one: a 2-1 comeback win over Leeds at the Emirates, with Bruno Guimarães scoring a late winner after Leeds had taken the lead. BBC Sport, Sky Sports, the Guardian, Opta Analyst and FourFourTwo all filed independent reports, making it the most widely confirmed item in today's feed. BBC Sport also reported a Hincapié injury in the aftermath, adding to what it called a growing list of fitness issues at the club.

Transfer chatter touching two of the six clubs stayed unconfirmed. BBC's gossip column and Transfermarkt's live blog separately linked Real Madrid with Scott McTominay and Michael Olise, with Chelsea tied to Frenkie de Jong — no third outlet corroborated it. Transfermarkt also reported that Bayern released a statement on Harry Kane's contract situation, after an earlier gossip-column report he was close to a new deal; the feed doesn't say what the statement contained. A separate Arsenal-Mora rumour was tagged 'also: BBC Sport,' but that's the same newsroom as BBC Gossip, not real corroboration.

Looking ahead, two of the six clubs meet Sunday: Liverpool host Manchester City at Anfield, a fixture Opta Analyst previewed twice, calling it the worst place City 'could possibly go.' The outlet also highlighted Liverpool's Jérémy Jacquet, a new defender it says has had a strong start without the usual settling-in period. Both are previews, not results — the feed contains no report of the match itself having been played.
